JJ Gabriel, 15, Asks to Leave Manchester United as Club Fight to Keep Highly Rated Prospect

Published 15 September 2026 Manchester United / Latest News TV96 Live Editorial Team Breaking news · 5 min read
Back to News & Guides

BBC Sport reports that JJ Gabriel has requested the cancellation of his Manchester United registration, but his departure has not been completed. The 15-year-old academy forward has reportedly sent formal notice seeking its immediate cancellation. United can challenge the request and, according to the reporting, have not abandoned efforts to resolve the situation with his family.

Gabriel had been considered a possible option for United's Carabao Cup match against Brighton, but is now not expected to feature. A request about registration, a selection decision and a transfer to another club are separate events; none should be treated as proof that a move has already happened.

What has happened?

BBC Sport says Gabriel has formally asked United to cancel his registration with immediate effect. The request creates a dispute about his status rather than an automatic release. United are able to contest it, and the outcome depends on what the relevant parties decide next. There has been no confirmation that his registration has been cancelled or that another club has signed him.

The precise reasons for the request have not been publicly disclosed. BBC Sport reports problems in the relationship between Gabriel's family and Manchester United, but that broad description does not establish the cause, the positions of each side or the terms of any possible resolution. It would be misleading to turn an incomplete account into a firm explanation of why the teenager wants to leave.

According to the BBC's reporting, Gabriel did not train with Michael Carrick's squad at the end of the previous week. That fact does not, by itself, explain the present disagreement. Reports also say that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are involved in discussions with the family. Their involvement underlines the importance United attach to finding a way forward, without amounting to a public club statement that an agreement is close.

Why Manchester United want to keep Gabriel

Gabriel is regarded as one of United's most promising academy forwards. His progress has put him near the first-team conversation before his 16th birthday, which falls on 6 October. Losing him would affect more than a single cup-team decision and disrupt a pathway that had begun to include senior exposure.

That pathway is delicate. Training with senior players and appearing in a match squad can accelerate learning, but regular competitive minutes at youth level remain valuable. A club trying to keep a young prospect has to explain how those opportunities fit together. That is a general development question, not evidence that playing time caused this particular dispute. For broader context on the league season around United, see TV96 Live's Premier League guide.

Gabriel's rapid rise

Gabriel scored twice on his Manchester United Under-18 debut when he was 14. Last season he was part of the United team that reached both the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under-18 finals. He also won the Premier League Under-18 Player of the Year award and United's own Under-18 Player of the Year award. Those honours reflect a strong academy season; they do not settle what his next step must be.

United gave him a senior pre-season appearance against Atlético Madrid in Stockholm. More recently, he scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut. The two milestones show that he has been exposed to different levels of football, from a senior friendly to a European youth match. Neither guarantees a competitive first-team debut or changes the need to manage a 15-year-old's development carefully.

Ryan Giggs' advice before the exit request

Before the current reported request, Ryan Giggs discussed Gabriel's development in comments covered by the Manchester Evening News. Giggs argued that United offered a strong environment for the teenager and stressed the value of both first-team exposure and enough actual playing minutes. His point was about helping a young player grow through training and matches, rather than treating a place near the senior squad as the whole answer.

Those remarks came before the latest development. They should not be read as Giggs responding to Gabriel's request, taking a side in the reported family-club disagreement or knowing its undisclosed cause. They provide context for the development choices United had been facing, not an explanation of the present dispute.

What happens next?

United and Gabriel's family can continue talks while the club considers how to respond to the registration request. BBC Sport reports that United have not given up hope of resolving matters. A request to cancel registration does not establish that a transfer is being negotiated or that Gabriel is available to sign elsewhere.

The immediate football question is his involvement against Brighton. Reporting now points away from an appearance in that Carabao Cup match, despite earlier expectations that he could be in contention. Readers can check TV96 Live's Matches page for fixture information, but an official squad announcement and the registration outcome will need to be assessed separately.

Where the story stands

The reported scope of the story is limited: a highly rated academy player has requested cancellation of his United registration, according to BBC Sport, and the club is reported to be trying to keep him. The reasons remain private and the outcome remains open. Until United, Gabriel's representatives or the relevant authorities confirm a decision, this is a request to leave, not a completed departure or transfer.
